assertions.name: cost_is_gram_row
assertions.detail: t_j = G_0j for all j, with b_0 = 1 (so i_0 = 0)

assertions.name: det_zero_exactly
assertions.detail: det G = 0 — identically zero in Q(q), not small

assertions.name: radical_annihilated
assertions.detail: sum_j G_ij v_j = 0 for every i

assertions.name: one_dot_v_factors
assertions.detail: <1,v> = -(q-1)(q^2-q+1); q^2-q+1 has no real root, so <1,v> = 0 iff q = 1

assertions.name: t_dot_v_zero
assertions.detail: <t,v> = (Gv)_0 = 0 — automatic once t is a row of G

assertions.name: certificate_dual_feasible
assertions.detail: y_0 = 0, s = e_0 satisfies t_j = y_0 + sum_i s_i G_ij, and e_0 >= 0

assertions.name: certificate_unique_for_positive_q
assertions.detail: s_1 = lam q^2 >= 0 forces lam >= 0; s_3 = -lam q >= 0 forces lam <= 0; so lam = 0 whenever q > 0. The certificate is unique.

assertions.name: x_star_meets_net
assertions.detail: sum_i x*_i = c <1,v> = n_target (shown at n_target = 1; c scales linearly)

assertions.name: x_star_constraints_tight
assertions.detail: (Gx*)_i = 0 for every i — feasible, every Frobenius constraint tight

assertions.name: x_star_objective_zero
assertions.detail: sum_i t_i x*_i = 0 = n_target * y_0 — the zero-gap identity, with both sides zero

assertions.name: h2_cost_is_gram_row
assertions.detail: t_j = G_0j here too — the certificate y_0 = 0, s = e_0 exists for H_2 as well

assertions.name: h2_nonsingular
assertions.detail: det G = (q^4 + q^2 + 1)/(q^4 + 2*q^2 + 1) — nonzero, so no radical

assertions.name: h2_no_forcing
assertions.detail: nullity 0: nothing forces y_0, so H_2 admits a one-parameter family of dual-feasible y_0. The degeneracy is an H_3 fact, not an artifact of the LP formulation.

description: Dual-certificate existence for the operator-selection LP, exact in Q(q). Bean qou/k4f8 stage 2. Self-contained rational-function arithmetic (fractions.Fraction, polynomial gcd, canonical normal form) — no numpy, mpmath or pyhecke in the computation, because the question turns on whether det G is ZERO rather than small: gram.py records |lambda_min| = 3.9e-17 through its NF path at 60 dps, and np.linalg.inv returning ||G G_inv - I|| = 1.64 without raising. For H_3(q) (d = 6): t is row 0 of G structurally (b_0 = 1), det G = 0 identically, rank 5, radical v ~ (-1/q)^len(w_i) — the q-antisymmetriser — and <1, v> = -(q-1)(q^2-q+1) is nonzero for every q != 1, so y_0 = 0 is FORCED for every dual-feasible (y_0, s). The certificate y_0 = 0, s = e_0 exists and is unique for q > 0; the optimum is attained on the radical with objective 0 and every Frobenius constraint tight. For H_2(q) the Gram is non-singular, so the degeneracy is a fact about H_3 rather than about how the LP was written down. Each assertion names the Lean hypothesis it discharges in operator_selection_lp.lean, so the two sides can be audited against each other.
caveats: Exact in Q(q) and therefore says nothing about any pinned q_0 that a numeric solve would use — deliberately. The committed f64 solves (a-K-via-lp-dual-full, a-K-via-lp-dual-hecke-basis) agree: y0_star = -0.0, y_star = e_0, dual_obj = 0.

y_0 = 0 being ATTAINED needs only t = G e_0 (the basis contains the identity), not the radical — see dualCertificateExists_of_cost_eq_gram_row, whose sole hypothesis is ht. The radical is what upgrades attained to FORCED, which is what y_0_eq_zero_of_radical proves and what this script establishes for H_3. Bean qou/augu found 14 of the 57 committed witnesses carrying a y0_star report it zero, twelve with the e_0 certificate, including one whose Gram is invertible.
